chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Sinān, from Mismaʿ Kirdīn al-Baṣrī, who said:

I used not to eat more than one meal in the night and the day. Sometimes I would seek permission to enter upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and find that the table had already been taken away, so that I would not see it before him. But when I entered, he would call for it, and I would partake of the food with him, and I would suffer no harm from that. Yet if I followed one meal with food eaten with someone else, I could not settle and I could not sleep because of bloating.

So I complained of that to him and informed him that when I ate with him I was not harmed by it. He said: "O Abū Sayyār, you are eating the food of a righteous people; the angels shake hands with them upon their bedding." He said: I said, "And do they appear to you?" He then passed his hand over some of his children and said: "They are gentler with our children than we are with them."

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, the kunyah of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام in this narration
key_terms.الطَّعَامِ: food partaken of in the Imam's presence
key_terms.النَّفْخَةِ: bloating or stomach gas causing discomfort
key_terms.الْمَائِدَةَ: the meal spread or dining table brought for eating
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the angels, described here as being close to them
key_terms.صَالِحِينَ: righteous people distinguished by spiritual purity
key_terms.صِبْيَانِنَا: our children, referring to the children of the Imam's household
key_terms.فُرُشِهِمْ: their bedding or resting places upon which the angels greet them

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the angels' closeness to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام and the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a companion's experience of finding special blessing in eating with Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, such that the food caused him no discomfort, unlike food eaten elsewhere. The Imam عليه السلام explains this by referring to the righteousness of his household and the angels' nearness to them, indicating their spiritual rank and the unseen divine care surrounding them and their children.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Misma’a Kirdeyn Al Basry who said,

‘I did not used to increase upon eating once by the night and the day. So, sometimes I would ask permission upon vising Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and find that perhaps the meal would have been raised and I would not see it in front of him<sup>asws</sup>. So when I would enter, he<sup>asws</sup> would call for it, so I would attain with him<sup>asws</sup> from the food, and I would not be harmed by that (the food at all). However, whenever I ate the food with others (people), I was not able upon settling and could not sleep due to gasses (indigestion).

So I complained of what to him<sup>asws</sup> and I informed him that whenever I ate with him<sup>asws</sup> I am not harmed by it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Sayyar! You are eating the food of the righteous people<sup>asws</sup>. Then Angels shake their hands upon their<sup>asws</sup> furnishings’. I said, ‘And they appear to you<sup>asws</sup> all (Imams<sup>asws</sup>)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wiped his<sup>asws</sup> hands upon one of his<sup>asws</sup> children and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are kinder with our<sup>asws</sup> children than we<sup>asws</sup> are with them’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people has narrated has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Sinan from Masma‘ Kirdin al-Basri who has said the following.

“I used to eat one meal in twenty four hours. I would ask permission to see abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) at such time that I would expect that their table cloth is collected and they have fished their meal. When I would arrive he would ask to return the table cloth. I would find food in it but it would not harm me while if I would eat with others again I could not do so and it would become very difficult for me to sleep because of gases.

I complained about it before the Imam (a.s.) and said that if I would eat from your table it does not harm me. He said, “O abu Sayyar, it is because you eat from the table of the virtuous people. Angels shake hands with them on their furnishings.” The narrator has said that I then asked, “Do they (angels) appear to you?” He has said, “The Imam (a.s.) wiped his hand over one of his children and said, ‘They are more kind to our children than we ourselves are.”
